                            + "percentages. Default false.",
                    ],
                ]),
            tool(
                "export",
                "Starts writing the timeline to a file and answers AT ONCE with "
                    + "{export_id, path, status} — ⌘E, the export sheet's six controls (format, "
                    + "size, frame rate, quality, loudness, range) in the sheet's own "
                    + "vocabulary, all but the frame rate — this exports at the document's "
                    + "rate, or on gif and apng at the format's own rate (12.5 and 25 fps). The "
                    + "export is a job in the Export Queue, run one at a time behind any other "
                    + "export already there; status is queued or running. Follow it with "
                    + "export_status, which never waits — call it again after a pause until "
                    + "status is done, failed or cancelled — and stop it with cancel_export. "
                    + "The export_id lasts until Frame Job quits. Every refusal comes back "
                    + "from this call, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing "
                    + "folder, and a graphic clip whose module does not compile; a failure "
                    + "while writing comes back from export_status, failed with its reason "
                    + "(a graphic that fails during the export stops it with no file left, "
                    + "naming the graphic and the frame). The preset is the ENCODING only and "
                    + "the size a separate choice defaulting to the document's own, or on gif "
                    + "and apng to the format's cap; the core resolves both into concrete "
                    + "settings (container, codec, size, rate, range) and hands them to the "
                    + "same exporter the sheet uses, so an agent export and a menu export "
                    + "cannot disagree. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the "
                    + "container's extension is added when the path has none. In an HLG "
                    + "project (set_canvas output) hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, "
                    + "prores_422 and prores_4444 write HLG unless dynamic_range says pq or sdr, and every "
                    + "other video preset writes the project's SDR version. What the finished "
                    + "file holds is export_status's done answer.",
                [
                    "preset": exportPresetProperty,
                    "path": [
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Where to write, e.g. ~/Movies/cut.mp4. The folder must "
                            + "exist.",
                    ],
                    "size": exportSizeProperty,
                    "range": [
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": ["project", "in_out"],
                        "description": "What to write: the whole timeline (default), or just "
                            + "the in/out range set_range set — the sheet's Range popup.",
                    ],
                    "video_bitrate": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "Target video rate in BITS per second (8000000 is "
                            + "8 Mbps) — the sheet's Quality popup. Omit to let the preset's "
                            + "own encoder settings decide. Ignored by presets that carry no "
                            + "rate of their own: ProRes is fixed by its profile, and GIF and "
                            + "APNG have no bitrate at all. On av1 and av1_webm it is a soft "
                            + "cap: SVT-AV1 "
                            + "encodes at a constant quality matched to HEVC at this rate (HEVC's "
                            + "0.07 bits per pixel per frame when omitted), and the file usually "
                            + "stays under it; very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 "
                            + "times over. On vp9_webm it is a soft cap too: libvpx encodes at a "
                            + "constant quality matched to HEVC at this rate (HEVC 10-bit's in an "
                            + "HDR export), and the file usually stays under it; up to about "
                            + "1.15 times it was measured.",
                    ],
                    "audio_bitrate": [
                        "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                        "description": "Target AAC or Opus rate in BITS per second (192000 "
                            + "is 192 kbps) — the sheet's Quality popup. Omit for 192 "
                            + "kbps. Ignored where the sound is neither: ProRes, WAV and AIFF "
                            + "all write LPCM, whose rate is its sample format.",
                    ],
                    "loudness_lufs": [
                        "type": "number", "minimum": -70, "maximum": 0,
                        "description": "Normalise the whole mix to this integrated loudness, "
                            + "in LUFS — the sheet's Loudness popup, whose rows are -14 "
                            + "(streaming), -16 (podcast) and -23 (EBU R 128 broadcast). The "
                            + "export measures itself first and then applies ONE gain to "
                            + "everything, so relative levels inside the timeline are "
                            + "untouched and no limiter is involved. Omit not to normalise: "
                            + "the export still measures and still reports. Ignored where "
                            + "there is no sound to measure (gif, apng).",
                    ],
                    "peak_dbtp": [
                        "type": "number", "minimum": -20, "maximum": 0,
                        "description": "The true-peak ceiling that gain is capped against, in "
                            + "dBTP. The sheet fixes it at -1 and this is the knob for "
                            + "anything else. Because normalisation is gain-only, a ceiling "
                            + "with no loudness_lufs beside it would have nothing to cap and "
                            + "is REFUSED rather than accepted and left inert. When the "
                            + "ceiling bites, the file lands quieter than the target asked "
                            + "for and the result's capped_by_peak says so.",
                    ],
                    "burn_in_timecode": burnInProperty,
                    // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-5, HD-14).
                    "dynamic_range": [
                        "type": "string", "enum": ["hlg", "pq", "sdr"],
                        "description": "An HDR (HLG) project's picture on hevc_10bit, av1, "
                            + "av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 and prores_4444 — the sheet's Dynamic "
                            + "Range popup: hlg (the default; BT.2100 HLG, no Dolby Vision), pq (HDR10: "
                            + "BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², mastering display P3-D65 0.005–1,000 "
                            + "cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000, MaxFALL 0) or sdr (the SDR version). Every "
                            + "other video preset writes the SDR version; hlg and pq are refused "
                            + "there and in an SDR project, where sdr changes nothing.",
                    ],
                    // The sheet's Speed popup (spec §11 CX-2, CX-12 (2)).
                    "encoder_speed": [
                        "type": "string", "enum": ["faster", "balanced", "smaller"],
                        "description": "av1's and av1_webm's encoder speed — the sheet's "
                            + "Speed popup: faster "
                            + "(SVT-AV1 preset 8), balanced (preset 6, the default) or smaller "
                            + "(preset 4, the smallest file for the picture and the slowest). "
                            + "Refused on every other preset, vp9_webm included (libvpx has one "
                            + "speed).",
                    ],
                ], required: ["preset", "path"]),
            // Window ▸ Export Queue's row for the job (spec §11 #326).
            tool(
                "export_status",
                "How an export this launch started is going — Window ▸ Export Queue's row "
                    + "for it, read now: it never waits, so call it again after a pause. "
                    + "Always export_id, status (queued, running, done, failed or "
                    + "cancelled), path and elapsed (seconds since export was called, or to "
                    + "the finish once it has finished). running adds progress (0 to 1) and "

                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=out, start_new_session=True,
                env=bounded.child_env({"RC_AGENT_SOCKET": self.socket,
                                       "CFFIXED_USER_HOME": str(HOME)}))
        if mcp.wait_listening(self.log, self.socket, child=self.child, seconds=60):
            print(f"  instance PID {self.child.pid} at {self.socket}", flush=True)
            return mcp.MCP(self.socket, timeout=CALL_BOUND)
        return None

    def stop(self):
        if self.child is None:
            return
        self.child.terminate()
        try:
            self.child.wait(timeout=30)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            self.child.kill()
            self.child.wait()
        self.child = None
        mcp.remove_scratch(self.socket)


def attempt(client, tool, arguments):
    """One MCP call; a refusal is an answer, and so is an expiry."""
    if client is None:
        return {"ok": False, "error": "no instance"}
    try:
        # `export` answers an id since #326; the helper follows it to the file.
        answer = (client.export_with(arguments) if tool == "export"
                  else client.call_with(tool, arguments))
        return {"ok": True, "reply": answer}
    except mcp.ToolError as error:
        return {"ok": False, "error": str(error)}
    except Exception as error:  # a socket timeout is the expiry
        return {"ok": False, "error": f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"}


def project_of(client, project):
    got = attempt(client, "get_project", {"project": str(project)})
    return got["reply"].get("project") if got["ok"] and isinstance(got["reply"], dict) else None


def tool_message(error, tool):
    prefix = f"{tool}: "
    return error[len(prefix):] if error.startswith(prefix) else error


# ---- the probe --------------------------------------------------------------

def build_probe(sources=None, probe_dir=None):
    """`export_cancel_probe.swift` as `main.swift` over every other file in
    `sources`, through `swift_build.build`, with the app's `Fonts`,
    `Blank.mp4` and a `default.metallib` of `Compositor.metal` beside it, in
    `probe_dir`. Reused when every input is byte-identical to a cached
    build's. The binary, or None and why.
    `None` for either argument means the module's `SOURCES` / `PROBE_DIR`,
    read at call time, so an importer that sets them is heard."""
    sources = SOURCES if sources is None else sources
    probe_dir = PROBE_DIR if probe_dir is None else probe_dir
    probe_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    binary = probe_dir / "export_cancel_probe"
    entry = probe_dir / "main.swift"
    if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text() != PROBE_SOURCE.read_text():
        entry.write_text(PROBE_SOURCE.read_text())
    fonts = probe_dir / "Fonts"
    resources = ROOT / "app/Resources"
    if not fonts.is_dir() or (resources / "Fonts").stat().st_mtime > fonts.stat().st_mtime:
        shutil.rmtree(fonts, ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.copytree(resources / "Fonts", fonts)
    if not (probe_dir / "Blank.mp4").exists():
        shutil.copy2(resources / "Blank.mp4", probe_dir / "Blank.mp4")
    shader = resources / "Shaders/Compositor.metal"
    metallib, air = probe_dir / "default.metallib", probe_dir / "Compositor.air"
    if not metallib.exists() or shader.stat().st_mtime > metallib.stat().st_mtime:
        step = bounded.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metal", "-c", str(shader), "-o",
                            str(air)], 300)
        if step["rc"] == 0:
            step = bounded.run(["xcrun", "-sdk", "macosx", "metallib", str(air), "-o",
                                str(metallib)], 300)
        if step["rc"] != 0 or not metallib.exists():
            return None, f"the shader did not build: {step['stderr'][-400:]}"
    lib = ROOT / "core/target/release/libframejob_core.a"
    if not lib.exists():
        return None, f"{lib} is missing — run `cd core && cargo build --release` first"
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift_build.app_sources(sources) + [entry],
                                  output=binary, defines=["FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"], timeout=900)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        return None, (f"swiftc rc {error.rc if error.rc is not None else 'before running'}: "
                      f"{(error.diagnostics or ['(no output)'])[:6]}")
    print(f"  probe: up to date — {binary}" if built.reused
          else f"  probe: built in {built.seconds:.0f} s — {binary}", flush=True)
    return binary, ""


def mutant_sources(name):
    """(MUTANT_WORK/<name>/Sources, "") — `app/Sources/*.swift` copied with
    each of the mutant's `before` texts replaced exactly once — or (None, why)."""
    _, edits = MUTANTS[name]
    target = MUTANT_WORK / name / "Sources"
    try:
        shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)
        target.mkdir(parents=True)
        for path in sorted((ROOT / "app/Sources").glob("*.swift")):
            shutil.copy2(path, target / path.name)
        for file, before, after in edits:
            text = (target / file).read_text() if (target / file).exists() else ""
            if text.count(before) != 1:
                return None, f"{file} holds {before!r} {text.count(before)} times, not once"
            (target / file).write_text(text.replace(before, after))
    except OSError as error:
        return None, f"the copy could not be made: {error}"
    return target, ""


def run_probe(binary, package, tag, delay):
    """One probe run: its JSON answer (with `rc` and `expired`), or an error."""
    out = WORK / f"{tag}.m4a"
    got = bounded.run([str(binary), str(package), str(out), f"{delay:.3f}"], 400)
    answer = {}
    try:
        answer = json.loads(got["stdout"].strip().splitlines()[-1])
    except (IndexError, ValueError):
        answer = {"error": f"no answer: {(got['stdout'] + got['stderr'])[-300:]!r}"}
    answer["rc"], answer["expired"] = got["rc"], got["expired"]
    return answer


# ---- G1, G2 -----------------------------------------------------------------

def land(client, project, name, track, at):
    """`add_graphic_clip` polled for at most 5 s while the store sees the
    module land. The new clip, or None and the last sentence."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
    last = ""
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        got = attempt(client, "add_graphic_clip",
                      {"project": str(project), "name": name, "track": track, "at": at})
        if got["ok"]:
            clips = (project_of(client, project) or {}).get("clips", [])
            ours = [c for c in clips if (c.get("graphic") or {}).get("name") == name]
            return (max(ours, key=lambda c: c["id"]) if ours else None), ""
        last = got["error"]
        time.sleep(0.2)
    return None, last


def nest_kind(clip):
    source = clip.get("source") or {}
    return source.get("project") if source.get("kind") == "nest" else None


def run_gate(client):
    pkg = WORK / "gate.framejob"
    made = attempt(client, "new_project", {"path": str(pkg)})
    wrote = attempt(client, "write_graphic", {"project": str(pkg), "name": "gate",
                                              "source": GATE_JS})
    track = ((project_of(client, pkg) or {}).get("tracks") or [{}])[0].get("id")
    clip, why = land(client, pkg, "gate", track, 0)
    first = attempt(client, "nest", {"project": str(pkg), "clips": [clip["id"]] if clip else []})
    top = (project_of(client, pkg) or {}).get("clips", [])
    inner = [c for c in top if nest_kind(c) is not None]
    text = attempt(client, "add_text_clip", {
        "project": str(pkg), "track": track,
        "at": inner[0]["start"] + inner[0]["duration"] if inner else 0})
    top = (project_of(client, pkg) or {}).get("clips", [])
    texts = [c for c in top if nest_kind(c) is None]
    second = attempt(client, "nest", {"project": str(pkg),
                                      "clips": [c["id"] for c in inner + texts]})
    project = project_of(client, pkg) or {}
    nests = {n["id"]: n for n in project.get("nests", [])}
    top = project.get("clips", [])
    b = nests.get(nest_kind(top[0])) if len(top) == 1 else None
    b_nest = [c for c in (b or {}).get("clips", []) if nest_kind(c) is not None]
    a = nests.get(nest_kind(b_nest[0])) if len(b_nest) == 1 else None
    a_gate = [c for c in (a or {}).get("clips", [])
              if (c.get("graphic") or {}).get("name") == "gate"]
    shape = (len(top) == 1 and b is not None and len(b_nest) == 1
             and len((b or {}).get("clips", [])) == 2 and a is not None and len(a_gate) == 1)
    movie = WORK / "g1.mp4"
    exported = attempt(client, "export", {"project": str(pkg), "preset": "h264",
                                          "path": str(movie)})
    check("G1 (CONTROL) timeline nest clip → nest B holding a nest clip → nest A holding the "
          "compiling `gate` clip; export h264 succeeds and the file exists",
          made["ok"] and wrote["ok"] and (wrote["reply"] or {}).get("ok") is True
          and clip is not None and first["ok"] and text["ok"] and second["ok"] and shape
          and exported["ok"] and movie.exists(),
          f"new {made['ok']}, write {wrote.get('error', 'ok')}, clip {clip is not None} "
          f"{why!r}, nest {first.get('error', 'ok')}, text {text.get('error', 'ok')}, "
          f"nest {second.get('error', 'ok')}, shape {shape} (top {len(top)}, B clips "
          f"{len((b or {}).get('clips', []))}, A gate clips {len(a_gate)}), export "
          f"{exported.get('error', 'ok')}, file {movie.exists()}")

    broken = attempt(client, "write_graphic", {"project": str(pkg), "name": "gate",
                                               "source": BROKEN_JS})
    # The store's set changes when it sees the file; poll get_project's view.
    deadline, seen = time.monotonic() + 5, None
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        graphics = (attempt(client, "get_project", {"project": str(pkg)}).get("reply")
                    or {}).get("graphics") or []
        seen = [g.get("ok") for g in graphics if g.get("name") == "gate"]
        if seen == [False]:
            break
        time.sleep(0.2)
    sentinel = WORK / "g2.mp4"
    known = b"B1 sentinel " + os.urandom(64)
    sentinel.write_bytes(known)
    refused = attempt(client, "export", {"project": str(pkg), "preset": "h264",
                                         "path": str(sentinel)})
    message = tool_message(refused.get("error", ""), "export")
    after = sentinel.read_bytes() if sentinel.exists() else None
    check("G2 a `gate` that does not compile, two nests deep: export h264 is refused before "
          "anything is written — \"The export was not started:\" naming \"gate\" — and the "
          "sentinel's bytes are unchanged",
          broken["ok"] and (broken["reply"] or {}).get("ok") is False and seen == [False]
          and not refused["ok"] and message.startswith("The export was not started:")
          and '"gate"' in message and after == known,
          f"write ok={(broken.get('reply') or {}).get('ok')}, store sees {seen}, export "
          f"{refused.get('reply') if refused['ok'] else message!r}, sentinel unchanged "
          f"{after == known}")


# ---- I1 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

def write_standins():
    STANDIN.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    marker = STANDIN / "ffmpeg.exited"
    (STANDIN / "ffprobe").write_text("#!/bin/bash\ncat <<'EOF'\n" + FFPROBE_JSON + "\nEOF\n")
    (STANDIN / "ffmpeg").write_text(
        "#!/bin/bash\n"
        "for a in \"$@\"; do [ \"$a\" = \"-encoders\" ] && exit 0; done\n"
        f"trap 'touch \"{marker}\"' EXIT\n"
        f"sleep {FFMPEG_SLEEP}\n"
        f"cp \"{A_MOV}\" \"${{@: -1}}\"\n")
    for name in ("ffprobe", "ffmpeg"):
        os.chmod(STANDIN / name, 0o755)


def rewrapped_entries(prefix):
    try:
        return sorted(name for name in os.listdir(REWRAPPED) if name.startswith(prefix))
    except OSError:
        return []


def run_import(client):
    support = HOME / "Library/Application Support"
    if not support.is_dir():
        why = ("the instance did not start" if client is None
               else "the scratch home did not take")
        check("I1 the instance's scratch home took", False,
              f"{support} is not a directory: {why}; no import was made")
        return
    marker = STANDIN / "ffmpeg.exited"
    if marker.exists():
        marker.unlink()
    hexed = uuid.uuid4().hex
    stem = f"slow-{hexed}"
    fixture = WORK / f"{stem}.mkv"
    fixture.write_bytes(os.urandom(4096))
    pkg = WORK / "import.framejob"
    made = attempt(client, "new_project", {"path": str(pkg)})
    started = time.monotonic()
    got = attempt(client, "import_media", {"project": str(pkg), "path": str(fixture)})
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
    reply = got.get("reply") if got["ok"] and isinstance(got.get("reply"), dict) else {}
    path = Path(reply.get("path", "")) if reply.get("path") else None
    inside = (path is not None and path.suffix == ".mov"
              and path.resolve().parent == REWRAPPED.resolve()
              and path.name.startswith(stem + "-"))

    # Cleanup, whatever the call answered, before the instance stops.
    expired = []
    deadline = started + 120
    while not marker.exists() and time.monotonic() < deadline:
        time.sleep(0.5)
    if not marker.exists():
        expired.append("ffmpeg.exited never appeared within 120 s of the call")
    partial_deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
    while (any(n.endswith(".partial.mov") for n in rewrapped_entries(stem + "-"))
           and time.monotonic() < partial_deadline):
        time.sleep(0.2)
    if any(n.endswith(".partial.mov") for n in rewrapped_entries(stem + "-")):
        expired.append("a .partial.mov was still in Rewrapped after 10 s")
    for name in rewrapped_entries(stem + "-"):
        entry = REWRAPPED / name
        if entry.resolve().parent == REWRAPPED.resolve():
            try:
                entry.unlink()
            except OSError:
                pass
    left = rewrapped_entries(stem + "-")
    if left:
        expired.append(f"left in Rewrapped: {left}")
    fixture.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    check(f"I1 import_media of a {FFMPEG_SLEEP} s stand-in conversion answers ok after "
          f">= {FFMPEG_SLEEP} s: kind video, 640×360, a .mov directly inside Rewrapped; "
          "cleaned up",
          made["ok"] and got["ok"] and elapsed >= FFMPEG_SLEEP
          and reply.get("kind") == "video" and reply.get("width") == 640
          and reply.get("height") == 360 and inside and not expired,
          f"elapsed {elapsed:.1f} s, answer {reply if got['ok'] else got.get('error')!r}, "
          f"inside Rewrapped {inside}, cleanup {expired or 'clean'}")

def write_noise(path, seconds):
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as out:
        out.setnchannels(2)
        out.setsampwidth(2)
        out.setframerate(48000)
        chunk = 48000 * 4
        for _ in range(seconds):
            out.writeframes(os.urandom(chunk))


def build_noise_fixture(client):
    """The M fixture over MCP: the saved package, or None and why."""
    noise = WORK / "noise.wav"
    write_noise(noise, NOISE_SECONDS)
    pkg = WORK / "noise.framejob"
    steps = [attempt(client, "new_project", {"path": str(pkg)})]
    imported = attempt(client, "import_media", {"project": str(pkg), "path": str(noise)})
    steps.append(imported)
    media = (imported.get("reply") or {}).get("media") if imported["ok"] else None
    for _ in range(NOISE_TRACKS - 1):
        steps.append(attempt(client, "add_track", {"project": str(pkg)}))
    tracks = [t["id"] for t in (project_of(client, pkg) or {}).get("tracks", [])]
    for track in tracks[:NOISE_TRACKS]:
        steps.append(attempt(client, "add_clip", {"project": str(pkg), "track": track,
                                                  "media": media, "at": 0}))
    clips = [c["id"] for c in (project_of(client, pkg) or {}).get("clips", [])]
    steps.append(attempt(client, "set_audio", {"project": str(pkg), "clips": clips,
                                               "patch": {"noise_reduction": 1.0}}))
    steps.append(attempt(client, "save_project", {"project": str(pkg)}))
    failed = [s.get("error") for s in steps if not s["ok"]]
    if failed or len(tracks) < NOISE_TRACKS or len(clips) != NOISE_TRACKS:
        return None, f"fixture: errors {failed}, tracks {len(tracks)}, clips {len(clips)}"
    return pkg, ""


def run_cancel(binary, why, pkg, pkg_why, runs):
    if binary is None or pkg is None:
        reason = why if binary is None else pkg_why
        check("M0 (CONTROL) the uncancelled measurement", False, reason, instrument=True)
        check("M1 cancels during the measurement", False, reason, instrument=True)
        check("M2 cancel latency", False, reason, instrument=True)
        return
    control = run_probe(binary, pkg, "m0", -1)
    window = control.get("window")
    check(f"M0 (CONTROL) {NOISE_SECONDS} s of noise on {NOISE_TRACKS} tracks with noise "
          f"reduction: the uncancelled probe run is success with window >= {WINDOW_FLOOR} s",
          control.get("rc") == 0 and control.get("outcome") == "success"
          and isinstance(window, (int, float)) and window >= WINDOW_FLOOR,
          f"{control}", instrument=True)
    if not (isinstance(window, (int, float)) and window >= 0.5):
        check("M1 cancels during the measurement", False, "no measurement window from M0",
              instrument=True)
        check("M2 cancel latency", False, "no measurement window from M0", instrument=True)
        return
    seed = random.randrange(1 << 30)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    print(f"  M1 seed {seed}, delay in [0.2, {window / 2:.3f}] s", flush=True)
    answers, crashes, bad = [], 0, []

        delay = rng.uniform(0.2, window / 2)
        answer = run_probe(binary, pkg, f"m1-{index}", delay)
        answers.append(answer)

        crashes += crashed
        good = (not crashed and answer.get("phase_at_cancel") == "Measuring loudness…"
                and answer.get("outcome") == "cancelled" and answer.get("left") is False)
        if not good:
            bad.append(index)
        latency = answer.get("latency")
        print(f"    run {index:2d} delay {delay:6.3f} rc {answer['rc']} "
              f"outcome {answer.get('outcome')} phase {answer.get('phase_at_cancel')!r} "
              f"latency {latency if latency is None else round(latency, 3)} "
              f"left {answer.get('left')}" + ("" if good else f"  {answer}"), flush=True)
    print(f"  M1 crashes: {crashes} of {runs}", flush=True)

          not slow and len(known) == runs,

class Instance:
    def __init__(self, label, app, arguments=(), env=None, home=False):
        self.label = label
        self.dir = WORK / label
        tree_copy.remove_tree(str(self.dir))
        self.dir.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.log = self.dir / "instance.log"
        if home:
            (self.dir / "home").mkdir()
            env = {**(env or {}), "CFFIXED_USER_HOME": str(self.dir / "home")}
        self.launched = mcp.launch(str(proof_app.executable(app)), list(arguments),
                                   env=bounded.child_env(env or {}), log_path=str(self.log),
                                   timeout=900)
        self.client = self.launched.client

    def stop(self):
        self.launched.stop()
        mcp.remove_scratch(self.launched.socket_path)

    def complaints(self):
        try:
            lines = self.log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return ["the log could not be read"]
        return [line.strip() for line in lines
                if "Frame Job: " in line or "Svt[" in line or "SVT-AV1: " in line]


class Doc:
    def __init__(self, instance, name, width=640, height=360):
        self.client = instance.client
        self.path = str(instance.dir / f"{name}.framejob")
        self.client.call("new_project", path=self.path)
        try:
            self.call("set_canvas", width=width, height=height, fps=30)
        except mcp.ToolError as error:
            if "made no change" not in str(error):    # a new project is 1920 × 1080 at 30
                raise

    def call(self, tool, **arguments):

    def wait_export(self, export_id, seconds=None, interval=0.2):
        """Poll `export_status` until the job `export` queued is over: `done`
        answers the status (every key `export` answered before #326), and
        `failed` or `cancelled` raises `ToolError("export: <reason>")`, so a
        caller sees the failure the blocking `export` used to raise. Past
        `seconds` the job is cancelled and a `ToolError` names its status.
        `seconds` defaults to this client's own `timeout` (600 unless the
        script built it with its own), the bound the blocking `export` call
        was held to before #326, so a script with a longer bound keeps it."""
        if seconds is None:

        while True:
            status = self.call("export_status", export_id=export_id)
            word = status.get("status")
            if word == "done":

            if word in ("failed", "cancelled"):
                raise ToolError(f"export: {status.get('reason', '')}")
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                try:
                    self.call("cancel_export", export_id=export_id)
                except ToolError:

  existing cancel flag checked per frame by the pump and the queue, and the flush before

"""Rule H for the graphics spike: every child runs under a hard wall-clock
bound, in its OWN process group, and only that group is ever killed.

`run` drains stdout and stderr while it waits (`communicate(timeout=)`), so
a child whose answer does not fit a 64 KiB pipe cannot deadlock it — the
lesson `tools/proof/README.md`'s words-spike section records. An expiry is
an ANSWER (`expired: True`), never an exception."""

import os
import signal
import subprocess
import threading
import time


def child_env(extra=None):
    """The caller's environment without the AssemblyAI key, which no row
    here needs (the Makefile `unexport`s it for the same reason)."""
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY", None)
    env.update(extra or {})
    return env


def run(argv, seconds, cwd=None, env=None):
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        child = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env or child_env(), text=True,
                                 stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                 stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True)
    except OSError as error:
        return {"argv": argv, "rc": None, "stdout": "", "stderr": f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
                "seconds": 0.0, "expired": False}
    expired = False
    try:
        out, err = child.communicate(timeout=seconds)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        expired = True
        try:
            os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Codec export C6a (spec §11 CX-18): what one bundled-encoder export costs — its resident
peak above the instance's own, and its wall time — measured over MCP, per Export Queue key,
at 1080p and 4K. `ExportEncoderCosts.swift`'s two tables are transcribed from its table,
and `designs/codec-export.md`'s "## C6a" records the run.

Every run is one fresh instance of the app `proof_app` chooses (`RC_PROOF_APP`, Release for
the record), on a scratch socket, stopped by its own PID; nothing else is ever killed. Each:

  new_project; set_canvas <w>×<h> at 30 fps (output hlg for the HLG key); AV.mov imported
  and placed twice on the first track (0 and 5 s: 10 s, 300 frames); one render_frame to
  warm the compositor; the baseline `ps -o rss= -p <pid>`; then `export` (the key's preset,
  and encoder_speed on the AV1 rows) followed to `done` while a thread samples the RSS every
  0.1 s. delta = peak − baseline; seconds = the done answer's `elapsed`; the 1-minute load
  average is read at the export's start.

Keys: av1 and av1_webm at faster, balanced and smaller; vp9_webm in an SDR project and in
an HLG one; h264 as the AVFoundation control. Sizes 1920×1080 and 3840×2160.

  python3 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py [--app debug|release|<.app>]
                                                [--only av1:balanced,h264] [--sizes 1080,2160]

Writes `tools/proof/work/encoder-memory/<date>/memory.json` and prints the table. A run
that fails is a row with its error, never an exit; the script exits 1 when any run failed.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "graphics_spike"))
import bounded  # noqa: E402
import mcp  # noqa: E402
import proof_app  # noqa: E402

AV = HERE / "media" / "AV.mov"
SEC = 600_000
FRAMES = 300
SIZES = {"1080": (1920, 1080), "2160": (3840, 2160)}
# name → (preset, encoder_speed or None, HLG project)
KEYS = {
    "av1:faster": ("av1", "faster", False),
    "av1:balanced": ("av1", "balanced", False),
    "av1:smaller": ("av1", "smaller", False),
    "av1_webm:faster": ("av1_webm", "faster", False),
    "av1_webm:balanced": ("av1_webm", "balanced", False),
    "av1_webm:smaller": ("av1_webm", "smaller", False),
    "vp9_webm:sdr": ("vp9_webm", None, False),
    "vp9_webm:hlg": ("vp9_webm", None, True),
    "h264": ("h264", None, False),
}
EXTENSIONS = {"av1": "mp4", "av1_webm": "webm", "vp9_webm": "webm", "h264": "mp4"}
SAMPLE_EVERY = 0.1
EXPORT_BOUND = 900


def rss_bytes(pid):
    """The process's resident size in bytes, or None once it is gone."""
    got = subprocess.run(["ps", "-o", "rss=", "-p", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    text = got.stdout.strip()
    return int(text) * 1024 if text.isdigit() else None


class Sampler(threading.Thread):
    """Samples one PID's RSS every `SAMPLE_EVERY` s until stopped; keeps the peak."""

    def __init__(self, pid):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.pid, self.peak, self.samples = pid, 0, 0
        self.halt = threading.Event()

    def run(self):
        while not self.halt.is_set():
            value = rss_bytes(self.pid)
            if value is not None:
                self.peak = max(self.peak, value)
                self.samples += 1
            self.halt.wait(SAMPLE_EVERY)


def measure(app, work, key, size):
    preset, speed, hlg = KEYS[key]
    width, height = SIZES[size]
    label = f"{key.replace(':', '-')}-{size}"
    folder = work / label
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    row = {"key": key, "preset": preset, "encoder_speed": speed, "hlg": hlg,
           "width": width, "height": height, "frames": FRAMES}
    launched = mcp.launch(str(proof_app.executable(app)), [], env=bounded.child_env({}),
                          log_path=str(folder / "instance.log"), timeout=EXPORT_BOUND + 60)
    try:
        client = launched.client
        if client is None:
            row["error"] = f"the app did not listen ({folder / 'instance.log'})"
            return row
        pid = launched.child.pid
        doc = str(folder / f"{label}.framejob")
        client.call("new_project", path=doc)

        def call(tool, **arguments):
            return client.call_with(tool, {"project": doc, **arguments})
        canvas = {"width": width, "height": height, "fps": 30}
        if hlg:
            canvas["output"] = "hlg"
        try:
            call("set_canvas", **canvas)
        except mcp.ToolError as error:
            if "made no change" not in str(error):
                raise
        media = call("import_media", path=str(AV))["media"]
        track = call("get_project")["project"]["tracks"][0]["id"]
        call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=0)
        call("add_clip", track=track, media=media, at=5 * SEC)
        call("render_frame", at=2 * SEC, path=str(folder / "warm.png"))
        time.sleep(1.0)
        baseline = rss_bytes(pid)
        out = folder / f"out.{EXTENSIONS[preset]}"
        out.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        arguments = {"project": doc, "path": str(out), "preset": preset}
        if speed:
            arguments["encoder_speed"] = speed
        row["load_1min"] = round(os.getloadavg()[0], 2)
        sampler = Sampler(pid)
        sampler.start()
        try:
            done = client.export_with(arguments, seconds=EXPORT_BOUND)
        finally:
            sampler.halt.set()
            sampler.join()
        frames = (done.get("duration", 0) * 30) // SEC if isinstance(done, dict) else None
        row.update({
            "baseline_bytes": baseline, "peak_bytes": sampler.peak,
            "delta_bytes": sampler.peak - (baseline or 0), "samples": sampler.samples,
            "seconds": done.get("elapsed"), "bytes": done.get("bytes"),
            "written_frames": frames,
            "per_frame_seconds": round(done.get("elapsed", 0) / FRAMES, 5)})
        call("close_project", discard=True)
    except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, OSError, proof_app.StaleApp) as error:
        row["error"] = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
    finally:
        launched.stop()
        mcp.remove_scratch(launched.socket_path)
        try:
            complaints = [line.strip() for line in
                          (folder / "instance.log").read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
                          if "Frame Job: " in line]
        except OSError:
            complaints = ["the log could not be read"]
        row["log_complaints"] = complaints
    return row


def gib(value):
    return f"{value / 1_073_741_824:.2f}" if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else "—"


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="encoder memory and time (codec-export C6a)")
    parser.add_argument("--app", help="debug, release or a .app path (default RC_PROOF_APP)")
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated keys, of " + ", ".join(KEYS))
    parser.add_argument("--sizes", default="1080,2160", help="comma-separated, of 1080,2160")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.app:
        os.environ[proof_app.ENV] = args.app
    keys = args.only.split(",") if args.only else list(KEYS)
    sizes = args.sizes.split(",")
    unknown = [k for k in keys if k not in KEYS] + [s for s in sizes if s not in SIZES]
    if unknown:
        print(f"unknown keys or sizes: {unknown}")
        return 2
    try:
        app = proof_app.bundle()
        proof_app.require_fresh(proof_app.executable(app))
    except (proof_app.StaleApp, ValueError, OSError) as error:
        print(f"the app cannot be driven: {error}")
        return 1
    work = HERE / "work" / "encoder-memory" / date.today().isoformat()
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    physical = int(subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "hw.memsize"], capture_output=True,
                                  text=True).stdout.strip() or 0)
    machine = subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "machdep.cpu.brand_string"], capture_output=True,
                             text=True).stdout.strip()
    print(f"app {app}\nmachine {machine}, {physical / 1_073_741_824:.0f} GiB", flush=True)
    rows = []
    for size in sizes:
        for key in keys:
            row = measure(app, work, key, size)
            rows.append(row)
            print(f"  {key:18} {size}: " + (row["error"] if "error" in row else
                  f"Δ {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} GiB (base {gib(row['baseline_bytes'])}, peak "
                  f"{gib(row['peak_bytes'])}), {row['seconds']} s, load {row['load_1min']}"),
                  flush=True)
            (work / "memory.json").write_text(json.dumps(
                {"app": str(app), "machine": machine, "physical_bytes": physical,
                 "date": date.today().isoformat(), "rows": rows}, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(f"\n| Key | Size | Δ RSS GiB | Baseline GiB | Peak GiB | Seconds | s/frame | Load |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for row in rows:
        if "error" in row:
            print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {row['error']} |")
            continue
        print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} | "
              f"{gib(row['baseline_bytes'])} | {gib(row['peak_bytes'])} | {row['seconds']} | "
              f"{row['per_frame_seconds']} | {row['load_1min']} |")
    print(f"\n{work / 'memory.json'}")
    failed = [r for r in rows if "error" in r or r.get("log_complaints")]
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

ROOT = HERE.parents[1]

import bounded  # noqa: E402
import mcp  # noqa: E402
import proof_app  # noqa: E402

AV = HERE / "media" / "AV.mov"
SEC = 600_000
FRAMES = 300
SIZES = {"1080": (1920, 1080), "2160": (3840, 2160)}
# name → (preset, encoder_speed or None, HLG project)
KEYS = {
    "av1:faster": ("av1", "faster", False),
    "av1:balanced": ("av1", "balanced", False),
    "av1:smaller": ("av1", "smaller", False),
    "av1_webm:faster": ("av1_webm", "faster", False),
    "av1_webm:balanced": ("av1_webm", "balanced", False),
    "av1_webm:smaller": ("av1_webm", "smaller", False),
    "vp9_webm:sdr": ("vp9_webm", None, False),
    "vp9_webm:hlg": ("vp9_webm", None, True),
    "h264": ("h264", None, False),
}
EXTENSIONS = {"av1": "mp4", "av1_webm": "webm", "vp9_webm": "webm", "h264": "mp4"}
SAMPLE_EVERY = 0.1
EXPORT_BOUND = 900


def rss_bytes(pid):
    """The process's resident size in bytes, or None once it is gone."""
    got = subprocess.run(["ps", "-o", "rss=", "-p", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    text = got.stdout.strip()
    return int(text) * 1024 if text.isdigit() else None

    """Samples one PID's RSS every `SAMPLE_EVERY` s until stopped; keeps the peak."""

    def __init__(self, pid):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.pid, self.peak, self.samples = pid, 0, 0
        self.halt = threading.Event()

    def run(self):
        while not self.halt.is_set():
            value = rss_bytes(self.pid)
            if value is not None:
                self.peak = max(self.peak, value)
                self.samples += 1
            self.halt.wait(SAMPLE_EVERY)


def measure(app, work, key, size):
    preset, speed, hlg = KEYS[key]
    width, height = SIZES[size]
    label = f"{key.replace(':', '-')}-{size}"
    folder = work / label
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    row = {"key": key, "preset": preset, "encoder_speed": speed, "hlg": hlg,
           "width": width, "height": height, "frames": FRAMES}
    launched = mcp.launch(str(proof_app.executable(app)), [], env=bounded.child_env({}),

            return row
        pid = launched.child.pid
        doc = str(folder / f"{label}.framejob")
        client.call("new_project", path=doc)

        if speed:
            arguments["encoder_speed"] = speed

        sampler = Sampler(pid)
        sampler.start()
        try:
            done = client.export_with(arguments, seconds=EXPORT_BOUND)
        finally:

            "written_frames": frames,
            "per_frame_seconds": round(done.get("elapsed", 0) / FRAMES, 5)})
        call("close_project", discard=True)
    except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, OSError, proof_app.StaleApp) as error:
        row["error"] = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"

        mcp.remove_scratch(launched.socket_path)

            complaints = [line.strip() for line in
                          (folder / "instance.log").read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
                          if "Frame Job: " in line]
        except OSError:
            complaints = ["the log could not be read"]
        row["log_complaints"] = complaints
    return row


def gib(value):
    return f"{value / 1_073_741_824:.2f}" if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else "—"


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="encoder memory and time (codec-export C6a)")
    parser.add_argument("--app", help="debug, release or a .app path (default RC_PROOF_APP)")
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated keys, of " + ", ".join(KEYS))
    parser.add_argument("--sizes", default="1080,2160", help="comma-separated, of 1080,2160")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.app:
        os.environ[proof_app.ENV] = args.app
    keys = args.only.split(",") if args.only else list(KEYS)
    sizes = args.sizes.split(",")
    unknown = [k for k in keys if k not in KEYS] + [s for s in sizes if s not in SIZES]

        print(f"unknown keys or sizes: {unknown}")
        return 2

        app = proof_app.bundle()
        proof_app.require_fresh(proof_app.executable(app))
    except (proof_app.StaleApp, ValueError, OSError) as error:
        print(f"the app cannot be driven: {error}")
        return 1

    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    physical = int(subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "hw.memsize"], capture_output=True,
                                  text=True).stdout.strip() or 0)
    machine = subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "machdep.cpu.brand_string"], capture_output=True,
                             text=True).stdout.strip()
    print(f"app {app}\nmachine {machine}, {physical / 1_073_741_824:.0f} GiB", flush=True)
    rows = []
    for size in sizes:
        for key in keys:
            row = measure(app, work, key, size)
            rows.append(row)
            print(f"  {key:18} {size}: " + (row["error"] if "error" in row else
                  f"Δ {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} GiB (base {gib(row['baseline_bytes'])}, peak "
                  f"{gib(row['peak_bytes'])}), {row['seconds']} s, load {row['load_1min']}"),
                  flush=True)
            (work / "memory.json").write_text(json.dumps(
                {"app": str(app), "machine": machine, "physical_bytes": physical,
                 "date": date.today().isoformat(), "rows": rows}, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(f"\n| Key | Size | Δ RSS GiB | Baseline GiB | Peak GiB | Seconds | s/frame | Load |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for row in rows:
        if "error" in row:
            print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {row['error']} |")
            continue
        print(f"| {row['key']} | {row['width']}×{row['height']} | {gib(row['delta_bytes'])} | "
              f"{gib(row['baseline_bytes'])} | {gib(row['peak_bytes'])} | {row['seconds']} | "
              f"{row['per_frame_seconds']} | {row['load_1min']} |")
    print(f"\n{work / 'memory.json'}")
    failed = [r for r in rows if "error" in r or r.get("log_complaints")]
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

an HLG one; h264 as the AVFoundation control. Sizes 1920×1080 and 3840×2160.

the lower of two calibrations: (a) the spike's gh5, promo and real8 through the spike's
     `vpxenc` (`--end-usage=cq`, the flags above, CQ 10–50 in steps of 2) against `crf.jsonl`'s
     HEVC rows, and (b) the owner's IMG_0018.MOV in an SDR project through a Release copy
     reading the CQ from a file, against `hevc`, both scored against `prores_422` as yuv420p.
     The 10-bit column is the owner clip in an HLG project at `hlg`, against `hevc_10bit` at
     `hlg`, scored as yuv420p10le. Each cell is the highest CQ reaching at least the
     comparator's VMAF under the real cap; a cell that misses is lowered by 2 until it meets
     the comparator or the cap binds. The measurements are (8).
  8. **The calibration** (`tools/proof/work/codec-spike/crf_vp9.py`, gitignored; rows `kind`
     "vpx" in `crf.jsonl`), 2026-10-28 on a shared machine. VMAF pairs the two files' frames
     by INDEX (`settb=1/30,setpts=N`): a WebM's block times are whole milliseconds, and
     libvmaf's timestamp pairing put a third of the owner clip's frames against a neighbour's
     (the first owner run read 76.17 at CQ 30 / Low where index pairing reads about 91; its
     rows lack `"align": "index"` and are not used). Each VMAF below is "CQ: VMAF (share of
     the cap)", the kept cell in bold.
     - **(a) The spike's clips** (vpxenc, 8-bit, against `crf.jsonl`'s spike HEVC rows,
       scored against each clip's own y4m as those rows were; a search of the grid, 81
       encodes): cells gh5 / promo / real8 — Low 46 / 34 / 36, Medium 38 / 30 / 30, Format
       default 34 / 30 / 26, High 32 / 30 / 24, Maximum 28 / 28 / 16. The largest cap share
       of the 81 was **1.143 ×** (gh5 at Low, at CQ 10 and 30, where the cap binds).
     - **(b) The owner's clip at 8 bits** (an SDR project, `vp9_webm` against `hevc` —
       91.141 / 94.415 / 95.469 / 95.777 / 96.85 — both against its `prores_422` as
       yuv420p): Low 36: 90.871 (0.712), **34: 91.568 (0.786)**; Medium 32: 92.880, 30:
       93.664, 28: 94.081, **26: 94.431 (0.867)**; Format default 30: 93.874, 28: 94.367,
       26: 94.811, 24: 95.215, 22: 95.375, **20: 95.498 (0.938)**; High 30: 93.957 … 20:
       95.753, **18: 95.882 (0.948)**; Maximum 26: 95.248 … 16: 96.844, **14: 96.993
       (0.912)**.
     - **(c) The owner's clip at 10 bits** (an HLG project at `hlg`, against `hevc_10bit` at
       `hlg` — 92.064 / 94.681 / 95.620 / 95.976 / 97.133 — scored as yuv420p10le): Low
       36: 91.907 (0.786), **34: 92.455 (0.852)**; Medium 30: 94.571 (0.790), **28: 94.897
       (0.848)**, 26: 95.164 (0.904); Format default 28: 95.316 (0.748), 26: 95.679
       (0.825), **24: 95.958 (0.893)** (kept after R3, below), 22: 96.066, 20: 96.145
       (0.948); High 26: 95.868 (0.775),
       **24: 96.198 (0.855)**, 22: 96.338, 20: 96.435, 18: 96.499 (0.946); Maximum 22:
       97.038 (0.700), **20: 97.234 (0.754)**, 18: 97.393, 16: 97.508, 14: 97.578 (0.890).

     | bits per pixel per frame (the 1080p30 rate) | 8-bit (Profile 0) | 10-bit (Profile 2) |
     |---|---|---|
     | 0.0386 (Low, 2.4 Mb/s) | 34 | 34 |
     | 0.0579 (Medium, 3.6 Mb/s) | 26 | 28 |
     | 0.0700 (Format default, 4.35 Mb/s) | 20 | 24 |
     | 0.0772 (High, 4.8 Mb/s) | 18 | 24 |
     | 0.1157 (Maximum, 7.2 Mb/s) | 14 | 20 |

     The owner's clip binds every 8-bit point (the spike's cells are 34 / 30 / 26 / 24 /
     16); every cell reached its comparator under the real cap, so no STOP. The guide, the
     MCP page and `video_bitrate`'s description name the measured maximum as about 1.15 ×
     the cap. The least margins kept: 8-bit Medium +0.016, Format default +0.029.
     **The 10-bit Format default cell was lowered from 26 to 24 at the first `--rate` run**
     (`vp9_export_proof.py` R3 on Release): that run's `hevc_10bit` Format default encode
     scored 95.692 (the calibration's, 95.620) and `vp9_webm` at CQ 26 the calibration's
     95.679, 0.013 under; by (7)'s rule the cell went down by 2, to the CQ 24 the
     calibration had measured at 95.958 (0.893 × the cap), +0.27 over either comparator. C2
     saw the same one-encode variance in VideoToolbox's `hevc_10bit` (CX-14 (6)).
  9. **The C wrappers.** `vpx_codec_enc_init` is a macro and `vpx_codec_control_` is variadic,
     neither of which Swift can call, so `app/Bridging/FrameJobVPX.h` wraps them in two
     `static inline` functions (`framejob_vpx_vp9_enc_init`, `framejob_vpx_control_int`).
  10. **An SDR WebM/Matroska copy is labelled too** (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-28 on
      C4's STOP; amends HD-18 (b) and HD-19 (b)). Measured in C4: Frame Job's own 640 × 360
      SDR `vp9_webm`, re-imported, rendered as BT.601 (cyan (0, 255, 255) read back
      (23, 255, 255); R/G/B 11.83 / 0.78 / 5.65 of 255 from the source's render), because the
      copy's description carried no colour and AVFoundation chose the matrix by the picture's
      size (the same round trip at 1280 × 720 read 0.53 / 0.16 / 0.30). So a copy whose
      Colour's transfer is neither 16 nor 18 now carries the labels its source states, from
      these sources in order, each field on its own:
      - **The Colour element:** `YCbCrMatrix` from MatrixCoefficients 1, 5, 6 or 9 (BT.709,
        BT.601, BT.601, BT.2020), `ColorPrimaries` from Primaries 1, 5, 6 or 9, and
        `TransferFunction` from TransferCharacteristics 1, 6, 13, 14 or 15 (the BT.709 class
        and sRGB), each the string Core Video names for the code
        (`CV…GetStringForIntegerCodePoint`), and none written for any other value or a code
        Core Video does not name.
      - **Else, for the matrix of a VP9 track, the first keyframe's `color_space`:** CS_BT_709
        is matrix 1, CS_BT_601 and CS_SMPTE_170 are 6, CS_BT_2020 is 9; CS_UNKNOWN and every
        other space write nothing. The core reads it with the `vpcC` it already builds and
        publishes it through `rc_container_describe` as `stream_matrix` (null when none); only
        Swift writes the labels.
      - **Neither:** the copy's description is unchanged, as before.

      The PQ (transfer 16) and HLG (transfer 18) copies are labelled exactly as HD-18 (b) and
      HD-19 (b) say. **Risk accepted:** an SDR WebM or MKV that was imported before reads
      differently now (its old copy in `Rewrapped/` keeps the old description until the
      source changes, the copy's name being a digest of the source); a label that lies is
      believed, as it is for every other movie.
  **Risks accepted:** VP9 is slow (about 39 fps at 1080p on the spike's M2 Max at cpu-used 4)
  and needs more bits than AV1 for the same picture; Profile 2 is decoded by fewer players
  than Profile 0; no player's HDR rendering was measured (CX-8); VMAF is not calibrated for
  HLG, so the 10-bit column's comparison is by the same instrument but not a perceptual
  claim; and the calibration covers four clips at 1080p.

- **CX-18 — C6a: the Export Queue's memory limit on bundled-encoder jobs, and the sheet's time
  estimate** (default, recorded in C6a before its code; amends #326's `queued` answer; the
  chain of road map 2's 7e and #326 is not touched):
  1. **The queue stays one job at a time** (#326, 7e): one `Exporter` on the main thread, a
     fresh one per job, `ReverseSource.pin` at most one. The limit is not a pool size; it is
     a hold on a queued job while OTHER bundled-encoder exports in the app already use the
     memory it needs.
  2. **The limit is app-wide over bundled-encoder exports** — every export whose settings
     carry a `writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, and C5's alpha row
     on arrival, since the rule keys on `writer` and not on a row id): the queue's running job
     and every Export… progress sheet's. They are booked in one main-thread ledger
     (`ExportEncoderLedger`) from just before the exporter starts to its finish.
  3. **The budget is a quarter of physical memory** (`ProcessInfo.physicalMemory / 4`), the
     share G-37 gives graphic rasters, so an export's two large consumers together stay within
     half the Mac. Relative to physical RAM, never a fixed figure (the owner's standing rule).
  4. **Each job costs its resident peak**, measured per key — preset, AV1 speed, bit depth
     (10 on `svt_av1`, CX-14; on `libvpx` 10 for `hlg`/`pq`, else 8) — at 1920 × 1080 and
     3840 × 2160 (`tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py`, the road map's "## C6a" record),
     and scaled by the export's pixels: proportionally below 1080p, linearly through both
     points above it, extrapolated past 4K. **A writer row with no measured cost costs the
     whole budget**, so it runs alone and nothing joins it, until it is measured.
  5. **A queued job is admitted** when nothing is booked, or when the booked costs and its own
     fit the budget. Otherwise it waits, and its row and `export_status` say why, in one
     sentence: "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about X GB of the
     Y GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about Z GB." A booking's end re-runs the
     queue.
  6. **An Export… sheet is counted but never held**: a person who chose Export… asked to
     write now, and waiting behind a hidden queue job would contradict the sheet's own bar.
  7. **A held job is passed over** by a later job the ledger admits — an AVFoundation job
     always — so a waiting AV1 job does not stall an H.264 one behind it; among AVFoundation
     jobs the chain's order is today's.
  8. **`export_status`**: `queued` adds `waiting` (the held sentence, present only while
     held); `queued` and `running` add `estimated_seconds` on a writer row. `export`'s answer
     is unchanged.
  9. **The estimate.** The export sheet's summary gains "Estimated time: about …" on a writer
     row: setup seconds plus the range's frames times a per-frame time scaled by pixels as in
     (4), from a per-key table whose every constant names its source. Rounded to 5 s under a
     minute, whole minutes under an hour, then hours and minutes. The constants are
     PROVISIONAL (one run each, on a shared machine) until C6b measures 4K on every row and
     the idle three-run speeds, which replace them by a table edit. No estimate on an
     AVFoundation row, in a queue row or in `export`'s answer.
  10. No format bump, no op, no `rc_*` export.
  **Risks accepted:** the cost is a measured peak on one machine and one picture, not a
  bound — a heavier timeline can exceed it; a sheet export can take the app past the budget
  (6); the estimate is a single-run figure until C6b.
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Codec export C6a (spec §11 CX-18): the Export Queue's memory limit on bundled-encoder
jobs, the held job's sentence, `export_status`'s `waiting` and `estimated_seconds`, and the
export sheet's time estimate.

The probe rows run `encoder_limit_probe.swift`, built through `swift_build.build()` over
`app/Sources` with `Blank.mp4`, `Fonts` and a `default.metallib` of `Compositor.metal` and
`ExportI010.metal` beside it, into `tools/proof/work/encoder-limit/probe/` (reused when
every input is byte-identical). It needs no app and no instance: its two live projects —
A1 (`av1_export_proof.av_doc`'s: 640 × 360, AV.mov from 0 under a two-second text clip) and
W9 (`webm_export_proof.long_doc`'s: 1920 × 1080, AV.mov 24 times at scale 3) — are built in
the probe from AV.mov, as `webm_readers_probe.swift` builds A1's. Every expected value is
computed HERE from P0's dump of the tables, in this file's own arithmetic.

  B0  the probe builds and answers (a probe that does not build is B0's FAIL, and every
      probe row's)
  P0  both tables dumped: the eight keys (av1, av1_webm × faster/balanced/smaller at 10
      bits; vp9_webm at 8 and 10), each figure positive with a source, 4K above 1080p
  R1  physical 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 GiB: budget = physical / 4, and per key at
      1080p and 4K the identical jobs admitted in sequence = max(1, ⌊budget / cost⌋), the
      cost the table's figure at the size
  R2  a writer row with no entry (`vp9_alpha_webm`, `libvpx`) costs the whole budget: it is
      admitted alone, then neither another of it nor an av1 job; an av1 job's booking keeps
      it out
  R3  an AVFoundation row (`h264`): no key, cost 0, `begin` books nothing, admitted beside a
      full ledger
  E1  `estimatedSeconds` per key at 1280×720, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, 3840×2160, 7680×4320
      and 150 / 300 / 1800 frames, and `sheetLine` its text
  E2  `estimateText` at 0.4, 2.4, 7.4, 57.4, 59.9, 60, 89, 90, 3569, 3570, 3600, 5399, 5400
  E3  `sheetLine` and `estimatedSeconds` nil for h264
  Q1  live, the shared queue and ledger, physical = 4 × the sheet job's cost: a headless
      Export… sheet writes W9 as `av1` Smaller; A (`av1`, A1), B and C (`h264`, A1) are
      enqueued. A waits with the exact sentence while the sheet runs; B then C run and
      complete before the sheet finishes; A launches only after the sheet's finish and
      completes; every file exists
  Q2  `AgentExports.track(A)` while held: status queued, `waiting` the sentence,
      `estimated_seconds` the table's
  Q3  physical 1 TiB, a sheet writing W9 as `av1` Faster: A runs before the sheet finishes
  Q4  `ExportQueueRowView.status`: the sentence for held A, "Waiting" for C while B runs
  Q5  the ledger is empty after Q1 drains, after Q3, after two `av1` jobs back to back (the
      second launched inside the first's `end`), after the queue refuses an empty
      project's `av1` job synchronously, and after a sheet does
App rows (`--app`, `RC_PROOF_APP`; instances in `tools/proof/work/encoder-limit/`):
  S1  File ▸ Export… on A1's project with `{"preset_id":"av1","encoder_speed":"smaller"}`
      pinned (`av1_export_proof.sheet_reading`'s pins): the summary label's second line is
      the table's "Estimated time: …"
  S2  the same with `{"preset_id":"h264"}`: no "Estimated" anywhere on the sheet
  X1  `export` av1 of A1, then `export_status` at once: `estimated_seconds` the table's; an
      h264 export's answer has none
  Z1  no instance log carries a `Frame Job: ` line

  python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py [--probe] [--app debug|release|<.app>]
                                             [--mutant NAME]

`--probe` runs B0–Q5 alone. `--mutant NAME` builds the probe over a copy of `app/Sources`
with the mutant's anchor replaced and runs the probe rows: exit 1 when every row it names
fails (CAUGHT), 0 when it survives, 2 when the control cannot be performed.

  no-hold           static `admits` always true: R1, Q1
  strict-order      `start()` stops at a held job: Q1
  sheet-uncounted   the sheet's `begin` removed: Q1
  no-wake           the queue's ledger observer removed: Q1
  budget-half       the budget physical / 2: R1
  estimate-flat     `value(pixels:)` answers `at1080`: E1
  no-waiting-key    `export_status`'s `waiting` dropped: Q2
  row-says-waiting  the row's `.waiting` status always "Waiting": Q4
  begin-late        the queue's `begin` after `exporter.export`: Q5
  token-overwrite   `finished` ends `ledgerToken`, then clears it: Q5
